skill.name: check-campaign-structure
skill.description: Check whether Google Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are built on the Product Metrics product segments, and read the results of the campaign plan. Use this skill when a merchant asks whether their campaigns or asset groups filter on the segments, where their Stars are served, why an excluded product still spends, whether a catch-all asset group serves every other product, how the segments compare with ProfitMetrics, Producthero, Channable, Flowboost or their own labels, or what happened since they applied the campaign plan. It reads the listing group filters, results per segment label and per campaign, and the plan results, then gives the exact steps to change in Google Ads; it changes nothing itself. It works through Product Metrics, so use it even when Product Metrics is never mentioned. Not for what the segments hold (check-product-segments), changing which custom label carries them (set-up-product-segmentation), or account trends and "why did ROAS drop" (analyse-google-ads).
skill.summary: Check how Shopping and Performance Max campaigns use product segments, and review results after a campaign plan is applied.
skill.author: product-metrics

content.value_statement: An exclusion or filter in one Google Ads group can hide where a product is still eligible to serve. Review targeting and segment performance with Product Metrics, then get steps for changes you can make in Google Ads.
actual_capabilities: Identify which custom label each campaign uses and whether it matches the Product Metrics segment label.
Find catch-all listing group rules and other asset groups where an excluded product is still eligible to serve.
Compare Product Metrics segments with third-party or merchant-defined labels and show examples where they disagree.
Report spend, conversion value, and return on ad spend by segment and campaign.
Compare campaign results and target return on ad spend before and after an applied plan, when results are available.
Provide steps for changes in Google Ads and recheck targeting after the user confirms the changes.
limitations: Live listing group checks require the Product Metrics MCP connection and access to the selected store.
The public API returns plan results, not the proposed plan. Open the Campaign plan page to compare the proposed structure with live settings.
The skill does not change listing groups, asset groups, budgets, or bidding targets.
Plan results are unavailable until the plan is applied and enough days have passed. The comparison does not establish causation.

use_cases.title: Check where priority products can serve
use_cases.description: Identify whether a Shopping campaign includes the Stars segment and whether a catch-all group also includes lower-priority products.

use_cases.title: Investigate spend after an exclusion
use_cases.description: Check other asset groups for the same product and use product-level reporting to verify whether spend continued.

use_cases.title: Review results after a plan rollout
use_cases.description: Compare campaign cost, conversion value, and return on ad spend before and after the plan was applied.

prompt_templates.title: Check one campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store], check whether [campaign] filters on the Product Metrics segment label. Tell me where Stars are eligible to serve.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an excluded product
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store], check whether [product name] can still serve outside [excluded asset group]. Show any reported spend for [date range].

prompt_templates.title: Compare two segmentation systems
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store], compare Product Metrics segments with [label name]. Show disagreements with recorded spend and give examples from [campaign].

prompt_templates.title: Review a campaign plan rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store], compare available campaign results before and after the plan. Include dates, currency, cost, conversion value, and past and current target return on ad spend.

output_examples.input: Does my Footwear Shopping campaign use Product Metrics segments?
output: Verdict: The Footwear Shopping campaign partly follows the segment structure.
The Stars ad group filters on the segment label. The All Products ad group has a catch-all rule that keeps other segments eligible.
Review the catch-all rule in Google Ads and exclude only the segments you intend to remove.

output_examples.input: Why did Trail Shoe 42 still spend after I excluded it from Core?
output: Trail Shoe 42 is excluded from Core but is still eligible in the Catalog asset group.
The product report shows USD 46 in spend from October 1 to October 7. That total does not identify the serving asset group.

output_examples.input: What changed after the campaign plan was applied?
output: In September, the campaign spent USD 800 and recorded USD 2,400 in conversion value. In October, it spent USD 900 and recorded USD 3,150.
Return on ad spend rose from 300% to 350%. The target changed from 280% to 320%.
The comparison describes the two periods. It does not show that the plan caused the change.

best_practices: Name the store and campaign before requesting a review.
Specify the reporting dates and check the currency before comparing spend.
Make one campaign change first, then ask the skill to verify the updated listing group filters.
anti_patterns: Assuming one asset group exclusion prevents a product from serving elsewhere.
Asking the skill to apply exclusions or adjust budgets directly.
Treating an increase in return on ad spend as proof that the campaign plan caused it.

faq.question: Which campaign types can I review?
faq.answer: The workflow covers Google Shopping and Performance Max campaigns.

faq.question: Can I check listing groups without MCP?
faq.answer: No. Live listing group checks require the Product Metrics MCP tools. The Product Metrics CLI can read feed settings and plan results.

faq.question: Can I compare my own custom labels?
faq.answer: Yes. Name the label you want to compare with Product Metrics segments and ask for examples of disagreements.

faq.question: Where can I see the proposed campaign structure?
faq.answer: Open the Campaign plan page in Product Metrics. The public API returns results, not the proposed plan.

faq.question: Why are plan results missing?
faq.answer: Results are not available if the plan has not been applied or if the reporting window has not matured.

faq.question: Will the skill change my Google Ads campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It gives you steps to follow in Google Ads and can recheck targeting after you confirm the change.
